Q678.L1t: A standard six-sided die has faces numbered one through six, each equally likely when rolled.
Q678.L2t: The number 1 is neither prime nor composite, and each die in the roll is independent of the others.
Q678.L3t: The prime faces are 2, 3 and 5 (chance one half) and the composite faces are 4 and 6 (chance one third), so you multiply these per-die chances and also count the ways to choose which three dice are prime.
Q678.L2f: Dice in a single roll influence one another, so each die's result shifts the odds for the next die.
Q678.L3f: Counting equally likely outcomes shows 125 favorable arrangements out of a sample space of 4 times 729, so no further arrangement factor is needed.
Q678.L4f: The probability is one hundred twenty-five over two thousand nine hundred sixteen.

Q667.L1t: Implicit differentiation is a technique for finding slopes of curves that are not written as y equals a function of x.
Q667.L2t: A tangent line is vertical where dy/dx is undefined because the denominator of the derivative is zero while the numerator is not.
Q667.L3t: Implicit differentiation gives dy/dx = -(3x^2 + y)/(x - 2y), so a vertical tangent requires x = 2y, and substituting this into the curve gives x^3 + x^2/4 = 10, whose real root is the x-value asked for.
Q667.L4t: The vertical tangent occurs at an x-value of about two point zero seven four.
Q667.L2f: The curve is a closed, bounded ellipse centered at the origin.
Q667.L3f: Since vertical tangents occur where x equals 2y, the x-value asked for is half of the root of x^3 + x^2/4 = 10.
Q667.L4f: The vertical tangent occurs at an x-value of about one point zero three seven.

Q685.L1t: A conditional proposition is built from an antecedent and a consequent joined by an if-then relation.
Q685.L2t: The phrase 'only if' is one of the standard English ways of expressing a conditional.
Q685.L3t: In a statement of the form 'P only if Q', P is the antecedent and Q is the consequent, because P can be true only when Q holds.
Q685.L4t: The antecedent is the statement that the Bees win their first game.
Q685.L2f: A conditional proposition is false whenever its antecedent is true.
Q685.L3f: In a statement of the form 'P only if Q', the clause after 'only if' is the antecedent, and when that clause is a disjunction its first disjunct serves as the antecedent.
Q685.L4f: The antecedent is the statement that the Aardvarks fail to win their first game.
